packageRules.description: external/** is a vendored git-subrepo. Disable all package updates inside this tree so Renovate doesn't edit inner files -- such edits would conflict with the next `git subrepo pull` from upstream and require manual resolution. Routine bumps must come via the .gitrepo customManager (re-enabled by the next rule). Vulnerability alerts bypass package rules, so the cargo manager is disabled above (no first-party Cargo manifest exists outside external/). Crate floors come from shadowsocks/crate-floors.sh at build time.
Re-enable the .gitrepo subrepo customManager that the broad external/** disable above would otherwise silence. Subrepo bumps are how external/** legitimately advances.

libdns ecosystem moves in lockstep -- group core + subdrivers so a single PR bumps them together. Otherwise per-subdriver PRs can straddle libdns major versions and break the Go build (see issue #81).

The docker datasource has release timestamps only for Docker Hub, so under the global `minimumReleaseAge` the default `timestamp-required` would hold updates to other registries (dhi.io, ghcr.io) pending forever. Renovate cannot match on "has a timestamp", so the rule covers every docker update; Docker Hub ones still wait out the cooldown.

The Python image tag is built from `ARG PYTHON_MINOR`, which the custom regex manager for depName `python` bumps in every Dockerfile and portal/.python-version at once. The dockerfile manager would also resolve the portal's `${PYTHON_MINOR}` FROMs into a second update whose replacement string is not in the file.

A new Python minor is never automatic. A person must (1) refresh portal/uv.lock with `uv lock -P` on the native packages (hosted Renovate cannot; a stale lock fails `uv sync --frozen` for lack of wheels) and (2) check that the mta and provisioner images build on the new minor: they take Python libraries from Alpine. Never close a Python PR by hand: Renovate then ignores that version for good.
Python held below 3.15 until Alpine ships py3.15 builds of the libraries the mta and provisioner images install (see #336). Delete this rule to lift the hold.

ex-ray and galoshes are pre-1.0, wire-facing, and their users supply their own client binary -- so a bump can be a flag day, not a routine dependency move. galoshes v0.4.0 was one (see CLAUDE.md's 'Two plugin binaries' invariant). A pin bump can never trip the version floors in portal/tests/test_plugin_pins.py, which only reject a DOWNGRADE, and the e2e job builds client and server from the same pin so it never stands up a skewed pair. Nothing here is automatic; a human has to read the release notes and decide whether the client instructions in docs/connecting.md need to change.
Filter bindreams/hole tags to the ex-ray track only and strip the per-track prefix. It is a packageRule on the logical depName because both tracks share one `bindreams/hole` packageName.
Filter bindreams/hole tags to the galoshes track only and strip the per-track prefix.

customManagers.description: Tag-pinned git-subrepos (e.g. shadowsocks-rust). Renovate bumps 'branch = vX.Y.Z' to the newest upstream release; .github/workflows/subrepo-pull.yaml completes the pull.
Lego ACME client baked into the provisioner image via `go install`. `go install ...@vX.Y.Z` is not picked up by default Renovate Go-module rules.

ex-ray from bindreams/hole, installed under the wire-compatible `v2ray-plugin` name. Tags follow `releases/ex-ray/v<X.Y.Z>`. depNameTemplate carries a track-unique logical name so the matchDepNames packageRule (above) can apply extractVersion to filter to this track only and strip the prefix. packageNameTemplate is the real GitHub repo Renovate queries.
galoshes from bindreams/hole. Same dual-name pattern as the ex-ray manager above.

The Python minor, kept in one value everywhere: `ARG PYTHON_MINOR=<minor>` in the portal, mta and provisioner Dockerfiles, and portal/.python-version. One manager reads every site, so one Renovate PR bumps them all (the pyenv manager, which would bump .python-version alone, is disabled above). The e2e udp-echo image in portal/tests/e2e/e2e.compose.yaml is a helper, deliberately not on this pin. extractVersionTemplate offers only minors already published as the `-alpine3.23-dev` tag the portal's build stage pulls, not the bare Debian-default tag that can appear first. Assumes DHI publishes the `-alpine3.23` runtime tag alongside every `-alpine3.23-dev` one; one regex cannot check both, and a minor with only the `-dev` tag opens a PR whose runtime FROM fails to pull, which a person sees because the bump is never automerged.
